summary: Warner Music Group CEO Robert Kyncl spoke at the Code Conference in Laguna Niguel, California, on September 26, 2023. He argued that labels stay relevant as music grows more complex and noisy, much as ad agencies survived Google AdWords. He expects AI to hit music first and be handled with a Content ID-style blueprint, said streaming audio is more resilient than streaming video, and said a slowdown in catalog acquisitions is fine because multiples fall.
one_line: At the Code Conference, Warner Music CEO Robert Kyncl explained why labels endure, predicted AI's near-term impact on music, and discussed streaming resilience and catalog deals.
key_facts: Robert Kyncl, CEO of Warner Music Group, previously served as Chief Business Officer at YouTube.
Kyncl's Q&A took place at the Code Conference in Laguna Niguel, California, on Tuesday, September 26 (2023).
Kyncl compared labels to ad agencies: when Google AdWords launched in 2000, many predicted agencies' deaths, but complexity and ad tech grew and agencies became among Google's largest customers.
Kyncl said that the more people can upload content, the greater the noise, making it harder to cut through and sustain a career, which is where labels add value.
Kyncl said artists need 'a team' and 'an army behind you' for a sustainable career with repeatability and success.
Kyncl predicted that 'within the next year' there will be lots of evolution around AI in music, with quality increasing at a very fast pace.
Kyncl said music digitizes first because it is short format, broadly distributed and well aligned with the internet, and that what happened to music 20 years ago is now happening in movies and TV.
Kyncl called YouTube's Content ID fingerprinting approach a 'blueprint' for AI-generated content, but said the technology for a Content ID-style system for AI is 'not yet developed'.
Believe CEO Denis Ladegallerie has said tools to recognize and flag AI-generated content are nearly ready and expects them within a few quarters.
Kyncl said music streaming will not suffer the problems of streaming video, noting 700 million people now in the world are in the premium subscription experience from zero 15 years ago.
Kyncl sees two growth opportunities: emerging markets with rising GDPs, and price elasticity optimization in mature markets.
Kyncl said the music rights acquisition market is 'likely slowing down a little bit', which is okay because it brings multiples down.
Warner Music Group owns the publishing catalog of David Bowie, bought a few years ago, and Kyncl said the company is in the business of both administering and owning rights.
